title: TUBE: Tangent Upper Bound on Evidence for Discrete Diffusion Language Models
claim: Likelihood is intractable and the ELBO bounds it from one side only; a tangent upper bound gives the other side.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, problem left, bound formula and plot right
description: Two dashed-border panels. The left panel has a blue header, 'LIKELIHOOD IS INTRACTABLE'. It shows masked-token grids for K decoding orders π(1)…π(K). Each grid unmasks tokens step by step, going down a time arrow t. Each order ends in a permuted sequence, and the sequences converge on the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat.' Below that is the marginal likelihood as an expectation over orders, then a note that 'ELBO gives only one side', with ELBO ≤ log p. The right panel has a green header, 'TANGENT UPPER BOUND'. It shows the sandwich inequality ELBO ≤ log p ≤ TUBE. An orange-boxed formula defines TUBE_ψ. Below it, a plot shows a dashed TUBE line tangent to the solid log p curve at p=ψ, with the ELBO curve underneath and shaded gaps between them. A vertical log-likelihood axis ranks log p_AR, TUBE, log p_model and ELBO.
caption: A tight tangent upper bound on log pmodel(x). Our TUBE bounds the intractable marginal from above using a tractable surrogate ψ, with equality at ψ = pmodel.
abstract: Log-likelihood is a standard metric for evaluating generative models. Unfortunately, in contrast to autoregressive models (ARMs), discrete diffusion models generally do not admit exact computation of this quantity. Existing evaluations, therefore, rely on the evidence lower bound (ELBO), leaving unclear how much higher the true value may be. We address this by introducing the Tangent Upper Bound on Evidence (TUBE), a variational upper bound on log-likelihood that admits an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator. Our TUBE extends across latent-variable models, including masked diffusion models (MDMs), any-order ARMs (AO-ARMs), and block variants of both. Applied to block MDMs and block AO-ARMs, TUBE reveals our key empirical finding that these models lie strictly below the exact ARM baseline, showing that ARMs still dominate in likelihood.
